title: Yara and the Alibi
premise: Sebastian Reyes, the concierge of the Grand Meridian Hotel, is handed a missing person's diary by a grieving sister — only to discover entries written after Yara Voss vanished, in handwriting that isn't hers. As Sebastian follows the diary's trail through the hotel's back corridors and the city's old money circles, he uncovers that Yara faked her disappearance to escape a powerful family's control, and that someone is killing to keep the 'closed case' closed. The diary's final entry points to an alibi forged years ago for a death everyone blamed on Yara's brother. In the end, Sebastian must choose between exposing the truth before the trial — which will destroy the hotel and the man he loves — or letting a lie stand; he finds a third path, turning state's evidence against the true killer while shielding Yara, who walks into the courtroom alive.
about_author: Lena Underhill spent a decade working night desks at grand hotels across three continents, collecting the stories guests thought no one overheard. She writes mysteries from a small apartment above a laundromat, where she still can't resist noticing everything.

chapters.title: The Guest Who Never Checked Out
chapters.summary: Sebastian Reyes, POV. A rainy Tuesday at the Grand Meridian: Sebastian notices a woman in the lobby who doesn't fit any reservation, leaves a package addressed to him, and vanishes. Inside is Yara Voss's diary. Emotional beat: unease — his perfect record of closed cases is about to be tested.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV. Reading the diary at 3 a.m., he finds meticulous observations of hotel life — then entries dated two weeks past Yara's disappearance, in different handwriting. He cross-checks dates against the police report. Beat: cold dread sharpening into professional obsession.

chapters.title: The Sister Who Handed It Over
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV. He tracks down Nadia Voss, who claims she found the diary in Yara's storage unit but admits she wrote nothing herself. She begs him quietly, off the record, because the trial of Yara's brother starts in six weeks. Beat: reluctant compassion; he takes the case no one wants reopened.

chapters.title: Back Corridors
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV. He maps the diary's references onto the hotel itself — service elevators, room 714, the wine cellar — realizing Yara worked here under another name the year before she vanished. Beat: the thrill of pattern recognition curdling as he realizes the hotel is complicit in something.

chapters.title: The Man in 714
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins: brief interludes from the diary's second hand, unnamed. Room 714's long-term guest, Aldous Wren, a family lawyer for the Voss empire, watches Sebastian too closely. Beat: first direct threat, delivered with impeccable courtesy.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV. Dinner with Elias, the hotel's night auditor and Sebastian's partner of three years, who warns him that Wren has already spoken to ownership. Elias asks him to drop it. Beat: tenderness strained by fear; Sebastian promises nothing.

chapters.title: What Everyone Swore Was Closed
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV. He pulls the old case file: five years ago, a body in the Voss boathouse, Yara's brother Tomas charged, an ironclad alibi supplied by — the Grand Meridian's own records. Beat: vertigo; his workplace is the alibi.

chapters.title: The Second Hand
chapters.summary: Diary-writer interlude, longer this time. The voice describes watching Yara rehearse her disappearance, devotion laced with resentment. Beat: intimacy turned possessive; readers sense the diarist loved Yara dangerously.

chapters.title: Nadia's Version
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV. Nadia reveals Yara visited her the week before vanishing, terrified, saying she'd seen something in the boathouse she was never meant to see. Beat: grief and guilt; Nadia withheld this from police out of family loyalty.

chapters.title: Pressure
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV. He's offered a promotion and a quiet transfer if he returns the diary; when he refuses, his access codes mysteriously fail and a falsified complaint lands in his file. Beat: institutional power flexing; isolation deepening.

chapters.title: Elias's Secret
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV. Following the alibi thread, Sebastian discovers Elias signed the night log the crucial evening — and lied about why he was there. Confrontation: Elias was paid to look away years ago, before they met. Beat: betrayal, love against duty made painfully literal.

chapters.title: Room Without a View
chapters.summary: Diary-writer interlude. The second hand describes keeping Yara 'safe' somewhere with no windows, insisting it was her idea. Beat: horror dawning — Yara may not have faked her disappearance alone, or willingly stayed hidden.

chapters.title: The Wine Cellar
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV. Acting on a diary clue, he searches the cellar and finds a hidden storeroom, recently used, with Yara's belongings and a second diary — hers, describing the boathouse murder she witnessed: not Tomas, but the family patriarch's fixer. Beat: the case cracks open.

chapters.title: Where Is She Now
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV. He realizes the second diarist is Marta, Yara's former best friend and fellow employee, who 'rescued' Yara and now won't let her leave. Racing the clock, he traces Marta to a shuttered sister property upstate. Beat: desperate momentum.

chapters.title: The House Upstate
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV. He finds the property watched by Wren's men — Wren knows Yara lives and needs her silenced before trial. Sebastian gets inside first and finds Yara alive but resigned, unwilling to testify and shatter what's left of her family. Beat: meeting the myth; her weariness humanizes everything.

chapters.title: Marta Unbound
chapters.summary: Yara, POV (first shift). Yara recounts her captivity-as-protection, her love for Marta warring with her need to be free, and her terror that testifying means becoming the family's target forever. Beat: claustrophobic tenderness; belonging as a cage.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV. Wren corners Sebastian with the ultimate bargain: Yara stays hidden, Tomas walks free on the existing alibi, and Elias's old crime stays buried — or everyone burns. Beat: the corrupting logic of power, almost seductive in its tidiness.

chapters.title: What Sebastian Notices
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV. Reviewing every detail one last time, he spots the flaw in Wren's plan: the original alibi required a second signature on the night log — Wren's own. Beat: quiet triumph; the observer finally sees the whole picture.

chapters.title: Six Days Before Trial
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. Sebastian brings prosecutor Nadia's evidence, negotiates immunity for Elias and protection for Yara, while Marta, cornered, nearly destroys everything by contacting Wren. Beat: highest tension; alliances fracturing under pressure.

chapters.title: The Alibi Breaks
chapters.summary: Sebastian and Yara, alternating. Wren's men close in at the safehouse; Yara chooses to walk out the front door and surrender to protective custody on camera, forcing Wren's hand. Marta confesses to the false diary entries to shield Yara. Beat: climax — courage over fear, love choosing freedom.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Courtroom chapter, mostly Yara's POV with Sebastian observing from the gallery. Her testimony dismantles the alibi; Wren is charged, the patriarch's fixer named, Tomas freed. Beat: catharsis; truth spoken aloud at last.

chapters.title: Checking Out, Checking In
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV, epilogue weeks later. The hotel settles its reckoning; Sebastian declines the promotion, reconciles with Elias on new honest terms, and visits Yara starting fresh elsewhere. A new mysterious package arrives at his desk — he smiles, and opens it. Beat: belonging chosen, not assigned; the door left open.
